Name: TENKAI MINI FARMER
Author: TENKAITENSHI
Description:
TENKAI MINI FARMER — TENKAI MINI GRANJERO
Author: Tenkai Tenshi | Version 1.8.0 | English / Español

A SMALL HELPER FOR YOUR FARM

Give your farm a companion that takes care of preparing the soil. Tenkai Mini Farmer adds robots with their own stations, independent work areas, and upgradeable tools. You choose where they work: they remove supported debris and re-till empty patches that lose their tilled state.

They do not replace every part of farming: they do not plant, water, or harvest. Their job is to keep the ground ready without removing your crops. They work on farms and in greenhouses while game time advances, from 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM.

GETTING STARTED

1. Buy a station from Pierre for 25,000g with the default settings.
2. Place it on your farm or in a greenhouse. A closed house needs a clear tile in front of its door; an open dock needs at least one clear exit.
3. Open its panel and choose the storage icon. Add ordinary Battery Packs.
4. Close storage: one pack becomes 500 charge. Additional packs stay stacked as spares.
5. Choose the assign-area icon and mark two corners with right-click or controller A. You may walk while selecting. ESC/B cancels.
6. Leave an accessible route. The robot will prepare supported tiles and store collected materials in its station.

Every station has its own area, charge, materials, and upgrades. You can place several. Work areas can be up to 32 × 32 tiles, with their center within 48 tiles on each axis of the station. Picking up and replacing a station preserves charge, upgrades, and appearance, but requires a new work area.

WHAT YOUR ROBOT CAN DO

• Till empty ground that the map allows to be cultivated, including patches that lose their tilled state.
• Remove supported small field stones, twigs, and weeds.
• Clear stumps, logs, and ordinary large boulders once the required tool upgrade is unlocked.
• Store collected resources in its station.
• Work in its location while the player is elsewhere, as long as game time is passing.

The robot checks each tile before acting. It protects living and dead crops, living trees, paths, machines, furniture, buildings, and other protected features. Large obstacles must fit entirely inside the assigned area. It does not break ore nodes or meteorites, and cannot make a tile farmable if the map does not permit tilling it.

BATTERIES AND RECHARGING

One Battery Pack supplies 500 charge. Tilling or clearing an ordinary tile costs one charge; large obstacles cost more. Protected tiles consume none.

On an open dock, the robot returns to its platform and sits down to recharge. The dock is empty while it is away working. When no spare packs remain, it sits without power and a notification appears. Adding packs reactivates it. Remaining charge survives saving, sleeping, and picking up the station.

UPGRADES FOR EACH STATION

Open the tools icon to upgrade that helper's hoe, pickaxe, axe, or motor. The menu uses real gold, bar, and Battery Pack icons, showing both required and available amounts. You confirm before paying. Materials may be in the station or your backpack; station materials are consumed first.

Tool tier | Gold    | Material
Copper    | 2,000g  | 5 Copper Bars
Steel    | 5,000g  | 5 Iron Bars
Gold      | 10,000g | 5 Gold Bars
Iridium  | 25,000g | 5 Iridium Bars

Hoe: from 1 basic tile to 3, 5, 9, and 18 tiles per use.
Pickaxe: faster work; Steel unlocks ordinary large boulders.
Axe: Copper unlocks large stumps; Steel unlocks large logs.
Motor: adds 5%, 10%, 15%, or 20% walking and working speed. Each level uses the matching gold and bar cost above, plus 1, 2, 3, or 4 Battery Packs, respectively.

THREE ROBOTS AND THREE STATION STYLES

Choose Original Robot, Farmhand Robot, or Seed Robot. The robot appearance applies to every helper through Mod Config.

Each station can have a different appearance: a seasonal house, an open wooden charging dock, or a metal charging dock. Load your save to see individual stations listed by location and coordinates in Mod Config. Changing their appearance preserves work areas, batteries, and upgrades.

Stations change with the seasons and decorate for festivals. Robots wear winter scarves and use lap blankets while seated. Their tools are small and held in their hands. Animations include walking, working, powering down, charging, greeting, and celebrating completed work.

A COMPANION WITH PERSONALITY

Approach a powered robot away from its station and it may lift its hat to greet you. Interact with it outside the dock to chat about the weather, date, festivals, or its work. Touching an occupied station opens its control panel.

ICON CONTROLS

Storage and batteries, assign work area, upgrades, pause/resume, show work area, and pick up station. Hover for help. With a controller, the focused action's name is shown. Empty storage before picking up a station.

REQUIREMENTS AND INSTALLATION

Requires Stardew Valley for PC and SMAPI. Tested environment: Stardew Valley 1.6.15, SMAPI 4.5.2, and Windows. The manifest declares SMAPI 4.1.10 as its minimum; use the current SMAPI release compatible with your game.

SMAPI: https://smapi.io/
Generic Mod Config Menu, optional and recommended for in-game appearance settings: https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098

1. Install SMAPI.
2. Extract the TenkaiMiniGranjero folder from the ZIP into Stardew Valley/Mods.
3. Install Generic Mod Config Menu if you want the in-game configuration selector.
4. Launch the game through SMAPI.

The mod generates config.json on first launch. It contains the station price, work per battery, global robot appearance, and individual station appearances. Content Patcher is not required.

LANGUAGES, UPDATES, AND COMPATIBILITY

English and Spanish follow Stardew Valley's language automatically. Other game languages use English as a fallback.

To update, close the game and replace the mod files while keeping your config.json. Keep the internal mod identifier unchanged: existing stations use it. Images include sprite presentations and demonstrations rendered by the game engine; they do not establish compatibility with every custom map.

The host manages robots and stations. Everyone should install the same version; multiplayer remains under validation. This version has not been validated on Android, consoles, macOS, or Linux. Custom maps must correctly identify farms/greenhouses and farmable ground.

If a robot is idle, check its assigned area, batteries, pause setting, working hours, storage space, and routes. Open/full storage and blocked paths can stop work.

Before uninstalling, empty and pick up every station, remove station items from inventories, save, close the game, and archive the mod folder. Do not remove it while custom stations remain placed.

CREDITS

Mod and mod sprites: Tenkai Tenshi.
